The fastest way to use Killer-Skills is via npx. You don't need to install anything globally.

Run a Skill

npx killer-skills add owner/repo

This command will:

  1. Download the skill from the registry
  2. Configure it for your current IDE (Cursor, VS Code, etc.)
  3. That's it! You can now use the skill.

Interactive Mode

Not sure what to do? Just run:

npx killer-skills

This launches the interactive menu where you can browse and manage skills.

title.ja: 使用方法とインストール

content.en:
To install AI agent skills with Killer-Skills, run npx killer-skills add owner/repo. The CLI works without a global install, detects supported IDEs such as Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code, and Windsurf, writes the correct skill format for that environment, and gives you a clean validation path before you standardize a wider workflow stack.

Recommended Path: Zero-Install via npx

For most teams, npx is the safest way to start. It removes global version drift, keeps onboarding lightweight, and makes it easy to repeat the same install flow across local machines, review environments, and operator handoffs.

PathBest forCommand
Zero-installFirst-time setup, testing, and team onboardingnpx killer-skills add owner/repo
Global CLIFrequent operators who run the CLI every daynpm install -g killer-skills

Install Your First Skill

  1. Open the project where your AI assistant should gain a new capability.
  2. Run the install command with the skill you want to add.
  3. Let the CLI detect your environment and write the IDE-native skill format.
npx killer-skills add owner/repo

The CLI is designed to bridge discovery and execution. If you are still deciding what to install, review the official trusted tools collection or the agent workflow building tools collection before you standardize a team stack.

Verify the Installation

Installation is only complete when you confirm the skill is present in the environment your team actually uses.

  1. Run npx killer-skills list to confirm the skill is registered.
  2. Check that the CLI wrote the right format for your IDE instead of falling back to a generic output.
  3. Open your assistant and confirm the new skill is available in the current project.
# Verify the skill is installed
npx killer-skills list

# Optional: inspect available commands
npx killer-skills --help

What the CLI Writes

Killer-Skills does not install one generic blob everywhere. It writes the format each environment expects so setup can survive real developer workflows.

  • Cursor: updates .cursorrules
  • Claude Code: installs into .claude/skills/
  • VS Code + Copilot: updates .github/copilot-instructions.md
  • Windsurf: writes skills into .windsurf/rules/

If you need the operator view of sync behavior, file outputs, and command coverage, continue into the CLI overview.

Common Commands After Install

# Install a skill
npx killer-skills add owner/repo

# List installed skills
npx killer-skills list

# Search for skills
npx killer-skills search "image"

# Open interactive mode
npx killer-skills

When Global Installation Makes Sense

Use the global CLI only when you already know Killer-Skills is part of your daily operator workflow and you want a shorter command path.

npm install -g killer-skills
killer-skills --version

Even then, keep the zero-install path documented for teammates and contributors who should not depend on a preconfigured machine.

Next Steps After Installation

  1. Use the CLI overview to understand sync behavior and environment-specific outputs.
  2. Use the official trusted tools collection when you need higher-confidence installs for a shared stack.
  3. Use the agent workflows solution page when the next step is solving a concrete multi-tool workflow, not browsing more repositories.

Installation FAQ

Do I need a global install first?

No. The recommended path is npx, because it keeps setup lightweight and current.

How do I know the install really worked?

Check npx killer-skills list, confirm the IDE-native files were written, and verify the skill is available inside your assistant.

What should I do after the first successful install?

Move into the CLI overview, a trusted collection, or an agent workflow solution page so you can turn installation into a repeatable operating path.

如果你要看更偏操作者视角的同步逻辑、文件输出和命令范围，可以继续进入 CLI 总览。

安装后常用命令

# 安装 skill
npx killer-skills add owner/repo

# 查看已安装 skill
npx killer-skills list

# 搜索 skill
npx killer-skills search "image"

# 进入交互模式
npx killer-skills

什么时候适合全局安装

只有当你已经确认 Killer-Skills 是日常高频操作链路的一部分，且希望使用更短的命令路径时，才建议全局安装。

npm install -g killer-skills
killer-skills --version

即便如此，也建议继续保留零安装路径，方便团队成员、协作者和新机器快速复现。

安装后的下一步

  1. 进入 CLI 总览，看清同步行为和不同环境下的输出差异。
  2. 如果你需要更高信任度的团队安装入口，进入 官方可信工具合集。
  3. 如果下一步是解决一个具体的多工具协作问题，进入 Agent 工作流方案页，不要继续盲逛仓库列表。

安装 FAQ

必须先全局安装吗？

不用。推荐路径就是 npx，因为它更轻、更稳，也更适合团队复现。

怎样确认真的安装好了？

检查 npx killer-skills list 的结果，确认 IDE 原生文件已写入，再到 AI 助手里验证 skill 是否可用。

第一次安装成功后应该去哪里？

继续进入 CLI 总览、可信合集或 Agent 工作流方案页，把“装好了”推进成“可复用的操作路径”。

Killer-Skills uses a modular architecture designed for extensibility and cross-platform compatibility.

Core Components

Skills

Skills are atomic units of AI capability. Each skill is defined by a SKILL.md file that contains instructions for the AI agent.

Workflows

Workflows orchestrate multiple skills to accomplish complex tasks. They define step-by-step processes that the AI follows.

Tools

├── workflows/

L'outil en ligne de commande Killer-Skills est un outil puissant et multiplateforme pour gérer les compétences des Agents IA. Il simplifie le processus de découverte, d'installation et de mise à jour des compétences sur divers environnements et IDE.

Capacités clés

  • Installation unifiée - Installation en un clic à partir de GitHub, du Registre ou de chemins locaux
  • Support universel des IDE - Configuration automatique de Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code + Copilot
  • Initialisation de projet - Création rapide de nouveaux projets de compétences avec des modèles
  • Gestion du Registre - Publiez et gérez vos propres compétences, des outils d'IA (Agents IA) personnalisés

Obtenir de l'aide

killer-skills --help

Pour obtenir de l'aide sur une commande spécifique :

killer-skills  --help

content.en:
Core Commands

add

Add a skill from the registry, GitHub, or a local path.

killer-skills add 
killer-skills add owner/repo
killer-skills add ./local-path

create

Create a new skill from a template.

killer-skills create my-new-skill
killer-skills create my-skill --template minimal

list

List all installed skills in the current project or global scope.

killer-skills list

search

Search for skills in the global registry.

killer-skills search "pdf processing"

update

Update installed skills to their latest versions.

killer-skills update

uninstall

Remove a skill from your project.

killer-skills uninstall

init

Initialize a new Killer-Skills project in the current directory.

killer-skills init

content.en:
Configuration File

Killer-Skills uses a global configuration file stored at ~/.killer-skills/config.json (or OS equivalent).

Settings

{
  "defaultIDE": "cursor",
  "githubToken": "ghp_...",
  "registryUrl": "https://registry.killer-skills.com"
}

Environment Variables

  • KILLER_SKILLS_HOME - Override the home directory for configuration and global skills.
  • GITHUB_TOKEN - Personal Access Token for higher rate limits when installing from GitHub.
  • DEBUG - Set to true for verbose logging.

Managing Configuration

You can use the config command to view and set values:

killer-skills config list
killer-skills config set defaultIDE vscode

content.en:
What are Skills?

Skills are the fundamental building blocks of AI agent capabilities. They define what an AI assistant can do and how it should do it. A skill essentially teaches an AI how to perform a specific task or set of tasks.

Skill Components

Frontmatter

YAML metadata that defines the skill's identity and triggers:

---
name: pdf-reader
description: Extract text from PDF files
triggers:
  - when user mentions PDF
  - when user uploads a .pdf file
---

Instructions (Prompt Engineering)

Measurements, guidelines, and step-by-step instructions in Markdown that the AI uses to execute the skill. This is the "brain" of your skill.

Tools (MCP)

Skills can optionally expose executable tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing the AI to interact with external systems.
content.zh:
什么是技能？

技能是智能体（AI Agent）能力的基本构建块。它们定义了智能助手可以做什么以及如何做。技能本质上教会了 AI 如何执行特定任务或一组任务。智能体工具（AI Tools）通常依赖技能来完成复杂任务。

技能组件

Frontmatter

定义技能身份和触发器的 YAML 元数据：

--- name: pdf-reader description: Extract text from PDF files triggers: - when user mentions PDF - when user uploads a .pdf file ---

指令（提示工程）

AI 执行技能时使用的 Markdown 指令、准则和步骤指南。这是您技能的“大脑”。

工具（MCP）

content.en:
What are Tools?

Tools are executable functions that an AI agent can invoke to perform actions in the real world, such as reading files, executing shell commands, or calling web APIs.

Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Killer-Skills leverages the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to standardize how tools are defined and exposed to AI agents.

Creating Tools

Tools are typically defined in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python and exposed via an MCP Server. A skill can reference these tools in its instructions.

// Example Tool Definition (TypeScript)
export const readFile = new Tool({
  name: 'read_file',
  description: 'Read contents of a file',
  parameters: z.object({ path: z.string() }),
  handler: async ({ path }) => {
    return fs.readFile(path, 'utf-8');
  }
});
content.zh:
什么是工具？

工具是可执行函数，人工智能智能助手（AI智能助手）可以调用这些函数来执行实际操作，例如读取文件、执行shell命令或调用Web API。

模型上下文协议（MCP）

Killer-Skills利用模型上下文协议（MCP）来标准化工具的定义和对人工智能智能助手的暴露方式。

创建工具

工具通常使用TypeScript/JavaScript或Python定义，并通过MCP服务器暴露。技能可以在其指令中引用这些工具。

// 示例工具定义（TypeScript） export const readFile = new Tool({ name: 'read_file', description: '读取文件内容', parameters: z.object({ path: z.string() }), handler: async ({ path }) => { return fs.readFile(path, 'utf-8'); } });
content.ja:
ツールとは?

ツールは、ファイルの読み取り、シェルコマンドの実行、Web APIの呼び出しなど、実世界でアクションを実行するために、AIエージェントが呼び出すことができる実行可能な関数です。

モデルコンテキストプロトコル (MCP)

Killer-Skillsは、モデルコンテキストプロトコル (MCP)を利用して、ツールがどのように定義され、AIエージェントに公開されるかを標準化しています。

ツールの作成

ツールは、通常、TypeScript/JavaScriptまたはPythonで定義され、MCPサーバーを介して公開されます。スキルは、ツールをその指示に参照することができます。

// ツール定義の例 (TypeScript) export const readFile = new Tool({ name: 'read_file', description: 'ファイルの内容を読み取ります', parameters: z.object({ path: z.string() }), handler: async ({ path }) => { return fs.readFile(path, 'utf-8'); } });
content.ko:
도구란 무엇인가?

도구는 AI 에이전트가 실제 세계에서 작업을 수행할 수 있도록 호출할 수 있는 실행 가능한 함수입니다. 예를 들어, 파일을 읽는 것, 셸 명령어를 실행하는 것, 웹 API를 호출하는 것 등이 있습니다.

모델 컨텍스트 프로토콜 (MCP)

Killer-Skills는 모델 컨텍스트 프로토콜 (MCP)을 사용하여 도구가 정의되고 AI 에이전트에 노출되는 방식을 표준화합니다.

도구 만들기

도구는 일반적으로 TypeScript/JavaScript 또는 Python에서 정의되고 MCP 서버를 통해 노출됩니다. 스킬은 이러한 도구를 자신의 지침에 참조할 수 있습니다.

Workflows sind mehrstufige Prozesse, die mehrere Fähigkeiten orchestrieren, um komplexe Aufgaben zu erledigen. Während Fähigkeiten atomar sind, sind Workflows molekular.

Workflow-Struktur

--- name: code-review description: Umfassender Code-Review-Workflow --- # Schritt 1: Code analysieren Verwenden Sie die code-analysis-Fähigkeit, um den Codebase zu scannen. # Schritt 2: Sicherheitsprüfung Führen Sie den security-scanner-Skill aus, um Sicherheitslücken zu identifizieren. # Schritt 3: Bericht generieren Kompilieren Sie die Ergebnisse in einen strukturierten Bericht.

Anwendungsfälle

  • Automatisierte Code-Reviews
  • Inhaltsgenerierungs-Pipelines
  • Datenverarbeitungs-Workflows
  • Test- und QA-Verfahren

Estructura del flujo de trabajo

--- name: code-review description: Flujo de trabajo de revisión de código integral --- # Paso 1: Analizar código Utilice la habilidad de análisis de código para escanear la base de código. # Paso 2: Verificación de seguridad Ejecute la habilidad de escaneo de seguridad para identificar vulnerabilidades. # Paso 3: Generar informe Compile los hallazgos en un informe estructurado.

Casos de uso

  • Revisión de código automatizada
  • Cadenas de generación de contenido
  • Flujos de trabajo de procesamiento de datos
  • Procedimientos de prueba y garantía de calidad

  • Les flux de travail de traitement de données

content.en:
Skill Structure

Every skill needs a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter:

---
name: my-skill
description: A helpful skill for...
triggers:
  - when user asks about X
---

# Instructions

When triggered, follow these steps:
1. Analyze the user's request
2. Perform the action
3. Return the result

Best Practices

  • Be Specific - Clear triggers help the AI know when to use your skill
  • Provide Examples - Show sample inputs and outputs
  • Handle Errors - Include fallback instructions

Publishing

To share your skill with the community:

  1. Create a GitHub repository
  2. Add your SKILL.md to .agent/skills/
  3. Submit a PR to the registry (optional)

content.en:
IDE Support

Killer-Skills supports a wide range of AI-powered IDEs and environments. The CLI automatically detects your environment and configures the appropriate rules files.

Cursor

Skills are installed into .cursorrules. The CLI appends instructions to ensuring Cursor's AI (Copilot++) can access them.

Windsurf

Support for Windsurf via .windsurf/rules/. Skills are created as individual Markdown files that Windsurf's Cascade can index.

VS Code + GitHub Copilot

Integration via `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. This allows GitHub Copilot Chat to be aware of your project-specific skills.

Claude Code

Support for Anthropic's Claude Code via `.claude/skills/`. This is the native format for Claude CLI.

content.en:
Overview

Killer-Skills exposes a metadata-oriented public API for directory integrations, filters, and CLI support. It is a machine-readable helper layer, not the canonical content surface of the site.

Canonical Content Rule

If you need installation steps, reviewed summaries, or citation-ready descriptions, use the public skill pages, collection pages, and docs pages on killer-skills.com. Public API responses may omit source files and long-form markdown.

Endpoints

List Skills

GET https://killer-skills.com/api/skills?page={page}

Returns paginated skill metadata for directory and app integrations.

Search Skills

GET https://killer-skills.com/api/skills/search?q={query}&category={category}&page={page}

Returns paginated skill metadata for search and filtering.

Get Skill Metadata

GET https://killer-skills.com/api/skills/{owner}/{repo}

Returns machine-readable skill metadata and a short summary. Use https://killer-skills.com/{locale}/skills/{owner}/{repo} as the canonical content URL.

Get Categories

GET https://killer-skills.com/api/categories

Returns lightweight category counts for directory navigation.

Indexing Policy

Public API endpoints are designed for applications and automation. They are served with X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow so search engines can drop historical API URLs while keeping the main site pages indexable.
